texts.preamble: Smt. Kamlesh W/O Late Sh. Darshan Singh vs Ramesh Chand Kohli S/O Sh. Kirpa Ram ... on 9 July, 2014 In The Court Of Ms. Ravinder Bedi : Presiding Officer, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal : Karkardooma Courts : East District : Delhi Suit No : 25/13 Unique Case Id No: 02402C0 040332013 1. Smt. Kamlesh W/o Late Sh. Darshan Singh 2. Praveen Kumar S/o Late Sh. Darshan Singh 3. Kaushal Singh S/o Late Sh. Darshan Singh All R/o B 85, Post Office Wali Gali, Shakarpur, Delhi - 110 092. 4. Smt. Kanchan W/o Sh. Swaraj Singh D/o Late Sh. Darshan Singh R/o A 2/149, Sector - 16, Rohini, Delhi 110 085. ... Petitioners Versus 1. Ramesh Chand Kohli S/o Sh. Kirpa Ram Kohli R/o. 1/3A, Jangpura A, New Delhi. 2. The New India Insurance Co. Ltd. Jeevan Building, Connaught Place, New Delhi110001. 3. Sh. Ravinder Kumar S/o Sh. Ved Prakash R/o 63/144, Village Alli, Badarpur, New Delhi. Mac Petition No. 25/13 Darshan Singh V/s. Ramesh Chander & Ors. Pag 4. Yogesh Kumar @ Titoo S/o Sh. Nemchand R/o Bansai, Po Onoda Distt. Mathura (Up) 2nd Add.: at Peepal Ka Gaon, Po Bilaspur, Bulandshahar. .....Respondents Date of institution : 22.04.2004 Reserved for orders : 01.07.2014 Date of Award : 09.07.2014 A W A R D 1. Initially, injured Darshan Singh had filed the Claim Petition under section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act claiming compensation for the injuries caused in a road side accident which occurred on 06.02.2004. 2.
texts.facts: Initially, injured Darshan Singh had filed the Claim Petition under section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act claiming compensation for the injuries caused in a road side accident which occurred on 06.02.2004. 2. Predecessor was [LEAKAGE_MASK] with directions to pass a fresh Award after giving an opportunity to the LRs of the injured Late Sh. Darshan Singh for their impleadment. 3. Pursuant thereto, by Order dated 26.04.2014 the legal representatives of Late Sh. Darshan Singh as petitioners were brought on record. Amended Memo of parties was filed and wife of deceased was examined as PW3. 4. The case of the petitioners is that on 06.02.2004 at about 3.30 p.m., MAC Petition No. 25/13 Darshan Singh V/s. Ramesh Chander & Ors. Page : 2/17 injured was going towards Shakarpur from Kalyanpuri. As he reached at Patparganj Road, in front of Mother Dairy, a bus bearing No. DL1PA 0477, driven by respondent no.4 at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, hit the two wheeler Scooter of the injured from behind. As a result of impact, injured fell down on road and sustained multiple injuries all over his body. A case u/s 279/337 IPC was registered vide FIR No. 77/04 at Police Station Pandav Nagar. 5. It is stated that injured was self employed and a claim for a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/ as compensation was preferred against the respondents. Ld. Predecessor after conducting an enquiry into the claim and providing opportunity to both sides passed the Award on 14.10.2009. The said Award was [LEAKAGE_MASK] by Hon'ble High Court Delhi vide order dated 15.01.2013 observing that injured Darshan Singh had passed away on 11.08.2009 and the Award was passed in favour of a dead person, which was unsustainable under law. 6. After hearing parties on the application u/o. 22 Rule 3 (1) CPC r/w. Section 151 CPC filed on behalf of Legal Representative of the deceased, all the LRs of the deceased were brought on record. 7. In the Written Statement filed by Respondent no. 1, it was contended that the offending vehicle was already sold by him to one Ravinder Kumar, i.e., respondent no. 3 on 04.06.2003. Thus, liability was denied on behalf MAC Petition No. 25/13 Darshan Singh V/s. Ramesh Chander & Ors. Page : 3/17 of respondent no. 1 on the ground of not having ownership of the offending bus as on the date of accident. 8. The respondent no. 2 in its Written Statement stated that the offending bus was insured with respondent no. 2 vide valid policy issued in the name of respondent no.1 Ramesh Chand Kohli, as on the date of accident. 9. In the Written Statement filed by Respondent no. 3, it was contended that he was owner of the bus and purchased it from respondent no.1; that the bus was insured with respondent no.2. 10.The respondent no. 4 in its Written Statement contended that no accident took place with the offending bus; that the offending bus was always mechanically checked by DTC. Rest of the averments of the petition are denied as wrong. 2 11.On the basis of the pleadings , following issues were framed by Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 14.06.2004 : 1. Whether the injuries sustained by the petitioner were caused due to rash and negligent driving of bus no. DL 1 PA 0477 by Sh. Titu S/o. Sh. Nemchand, owned by respondent no. 1 and insured with respondent no. 2? 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for payment of any compensation for sustaining such injuries, if so, to what amount and from whom? 3. Relief. 12.After impleadment of the respondent no. 4/Driver, one additional issue MAC Petition No. 25/13 Darshan Singh V/s. Ramesh Chander & Ors. Page : 4/17 was framed on 28.09.2007 : 4. "Whether petitioner sustained injuries due to his own fault and overload of his scooter, if so, to what effect?" 13.The injured was examined as PW1 on 09.05.2005. Respondent no. 2 / Insurance Company examined Sh. Rajender Kumar, Record Clerk, ARTO from Bulandshahar, UP as R2W1, who has proved record of Driving License no. T - 4553 , issued to one Manbir Giri and supplied to the Insurance Company which is as R2W1/2, summoned from the Court of Ld. MM Concerned. He stated that this Driving License was not issued by his Authority. Insurance Company also filed Affidavit of Sh. Pramod Rathore, Assistant to the effect that Insurance Policy was issued in favour of respondent no. 1,who had sold the offending bus to respondent no. 3 without giving information to the Insurance Company. As per affidavit of R2W2, Insurance Company also verified the DL of respondent no. 4/ Driver, who had driving licesnce allegedly issued from Bulandshahar Authority, but which on verification was found that it was not issued by the said authority. R2W2 also proved the notice u/o.12 Rule 8 CPC served by Insurance Company on Driver & Owner. 14.Respondent no.3 filed his evidence and examined himself as R3W1 on 18.08.2009. Similarly respondent no. 4 also filed his affidavit in evidence and was examined as R4W1, in which he stated that he had vast MAC Petition No. 25/13 Darshan Singh V/s. Ramesh Chander & Ors. Page : 5/17 experience of driving heavy vehicles and that the respondent no. 3 had verified the DL of respondent no. 4, while employing him as a driver. He has proved the DL as Ex. DW4/A. 15.I have heard As he reached on Patparganj road, in front of Mother Dairy, a bus bearing No. DL 1PA 0477, driven by respondent no.1 at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, hit his Scooter from behind and because of impact, he fell down on road and sustained fracture in his both hands and multiple injuries upon his face and legs. He denied the suggestion that his scooter MAC Petition No. 25/13 Darshan Singh V/s. Ramesh Chander & Ors. Page : 6/17 was overloaded by replying that it was not practicable to load goods on scooter as he was coming after taking some orders. 17.Driver/respondent no.4 has admitted of FIR having registered against him and criminal case pending before Ld. MM. He was treated there till 11.02.2004. He was readmitted in the same Hospital on 24.02.2004 and was discharged on 27.02.2004. He was operated upon and rods were put in his Right hand & plate was put in shoulder. He stated that his right portion of body had stopped working. 23.He sustained Permanent Disability up to 70% as per Ex. P1 in relation to his right upper limb and was operated twice for the same. Towards 1/3 of Loss of Earnings (Rs.85,978.20 x 1/3) Rs. 28,660.00 Total = Rs.1,89,897.00 Therefore, petitioners are entitled to Rs.1,89,900/ (rounded off) which shall be the just compensation to them. R2W1 was also shown the DL of driver/ respondent no. 4 from the charge sheet summoned from the Court of Ld. MM, to which he stated that this license was not issued by their authority and that it was a fake document. 34.Respondent no. 2 also examined Sh. Pramod Rathore as R2W2 who has proved the documents i.e. notice U/O. 12 Rule 8 CPC upon the owner as well as driver. He has proved verification report Ex. R2W2/2, of DL of Driver and stated that the same was found to be fake.
texts.arguments: In Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Guwahati High Court has observed as under : "In deciding a matter tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case. 18.In the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. , the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held as under : "8. In Bimla Devi and Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors., (2009) 13 SC 530, the Supreme Court held that in a petition under Section 166 of the Act, the petitioners were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition under the Motor Vehicles Act. Para 15 of the report is extracted hereunder : Smt. Kamlesh W/O Late Sh. Darshan Singh vs Ramesh Chand Kohli S/O Sh. Kirpa Ram ... on 9 July, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166813375/ 4 "15. It was to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the petitioners. The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied." 19.The report in Bimla Devi (Supra) was relied on by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in its later judgments in Parmeshwari v. Amir Chand (2011) 11 SCC 635 and Kusum Lata v. Satbir, (2011) 3 SCC 646." 20.In the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pushpa Rana & Ors. : 2009 ACJ 287 , the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that : MAC Petition No. 25/13 Darshan Singh V/s. Ramesh Chander & Ors. Page : 8/17 "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents - petitioners should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal (Supra). On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle; (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of chargesheet under Sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of F.I.R., wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased. case was noticed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case titled as Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh : 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310 where it was noted that there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in the case. Hon'ble Supreme Court enumerated the principles for granting the compensation payable to road traffic accident victims. In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr., MANU/SC/1018/2010, Civil Appeal No. 8981/2010 decided on 18.10.2010, following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims : i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner. Page : 10/17 ii) Compensation payable in injury cases is payable under two heads. In Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs. Lalita, AIR 1981 Delhi 558, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that there cannot be any deduction if domestic help is obtained from a family member. The Hon'ble High Court has observed as under : "...........A wrong doer cannot take advantage of this 'domestic element'. If the mother renders service to her, instead of a nurse, it is right and just that she should recover compensation for the value of the services that the mother has rendered to her. Mother's services were necessitated by the wrong doing and the injured should be compensated for it. (Cunnigharn v. Harrison 3 All E.R. 463). The services of a wife and mother are worth more than those of a housekeeper because she is in constant attendance and does many more things than a housekeeper. (Regan v. Williamson (1976) 2 All E.R. 241)." 28.This judgment was again relied upon by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Narayan Bahadur v. Sumeet Gupta and Anr., MAC MAC Petition No. 25/13 Darshan Singh V/s. Ramesh Chander & Ors.
